title: Nova X5 Review: Worth 25,000 Rupees?
audience: Indian buyers comparing budget smartphones around 25,000 rupees, many buying their first good phone.
brief: Help Indian viewers decide between the fictional Nova X5 and its rivals with prices and advice that apply in India. Keep it friendly and encouraging for first-time buyers. Goal: viewers join the Telegram deals channel at nova.example/deals for price-drop alerts.

issues.description: A string of unexplained spec terms (LTPO AMOLED, UFS 3.1, vapour chamber, PWM dimming, SoC binning) is used with no gloss for a general first-time-buyer audience.
Claims the battery 'easily lasts three days of heavy use' with no test, settings or source cited; a 5,000 mAh phone does not last three days of heavy use.
Gives the price only in US dollars and assumes US carriers and stores (Verizon, T-Mobile, Best Buy) although the audience and brief are Indian; the price should be in rupees with Indian retailers.
Sneers at budget buyers ('if you cannot afford a real flagship, I guess this is fine for you people'), which contradicts the brief's friendly, encouraging tone for first-time buyers.
Advises leaving the phone charging under a pillow overnight and says the warmth is normal. Phone makers warn against charging under bedding because trapped heat is a fire risk.
Opens by promising a camera comparison with the Pixel at the end of the video, then ends without any camera comparison.
